title: A Quick Recap of Integers

learningObjectives: Understand and solve number puzzles involving sum and difference of integers
Model integer operations using movement on a number line
Use the token model to visualize addition and subtraction of integers
Recognize that subtracting a number is equivalent to adding its additive inverse
Apply integer concepts to real-world scenarios

Solve problems involving temperature changes, banking, and elevation

keyTerms.definition: A whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero
The result of adding two or more numbers
The result of subtracting one number from another (first number - second number)
A visual representation of numbers on a straight line, with negative numbers to the left of zero and positive numbers to the right
The number that, when added to a given number, results in zero. For integer a, the additive inverse is -a
A pair of one positive and one negative token that cancel each other out to equal zero
A visual model using colored tokens to represent positive and negative integers
The absolute value or size of a number, without regard to its sign
In the context of integers, whether a number is positive (right/up) or negative (left/down)

practiceModeQuestions.question: If two numbers have a sum of 15 and a difference of 5, what are the two numbers?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: Using algebra: a + b = 15 and a - b = 5. Adding these equations: 2a = 20, so a = 10. Then b = 5.

practiceModeQuestions.question: A carrom coin starts at position 0. It moves 7 units right, then 3 units left. What is its final position?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: 7 units right is +7, 3 units left is -3. Final position: 7 + (-3) = 4

practiceModeQuestions.question: What is the additive inverse of -15?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: The additive inverse of a number is the number that, when added to it, gives 0. -15 + 15 = 0

practiceModeQuestions.question: Calculate: 8 - 12 = ?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: 8 - 12 = 8 + (-12) = -4. Starting at 8 and moving 12 units left lands at -4.

practiceModeQuestions.question: Which statement is TRUE about subtracting integers?
options: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite
You cannot subtract a larger number from a smaller number
Subtraction and addition are the same operation
practiceModeQuestions.correct: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: a - b = a + (-b). This is a fundamental property of integer subtraction.

practiceModeQuestions.question: If the first movement on a number line is -5 and the final position is 3, what is the second movement?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: Using P = a + b: 3 = -5 + b, so b = 8

practiceModeQuestions.question: In the token model, one green token and one red token together equal:
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: A green token (+1) and red token (-1) form a zero pair: +1 + (-1) = 0

practiceModeQuestions.question: Calculate: (-3) + (-7) = ?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: When adding two negative numbers, add their magnitudes and keep the negative sign: -3 + (-7) = -10

practiceModeQuestions.question: Two numbers have a sum of 0 and a difference of 14. What are the numbers?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: If sum = 0, the numbers are opposites. If difference = 14, then 7 - (-7) = 14

practiceModeQuestions.question: What is 5 - (-3)?
practiceModeQuestions.explanation: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 5 - (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8

realWorldApplications.title: Temperature Changes
realWorldApplications.description: Recording temperature changes in freezing processes, weather forecasting, and climate control
realWorldApplications.example: A freezing process lowers temperature by 5°C per hour. Starting at 8°C, after 4 hours: 8 + (4 × -5) = -12°C
realWorldApplications.formula: Final Temperature = Starting Temperature + (Hours × Change per Hour)

realWorldApplications.title: Bank Transactions
realWorldApplications.description: Tracking deposits (positive) and withdrawals (negative) in account balance
realWorldApplications.formula: Final Balance = Starting Balance + Deposits - Withdrawals

realWorldApplications.title: Elevation and Sea Level
realWorldApplications.description: Measuring heights above sea level (positive) and depths below sea level (negative)
realWorldApplications.example: Mt. Everest: +8,849m, Dead Sea: -430m, Mariana Trench: -11,034m
realWorldApplications.formula: Final Position = Starting Position + Change in Elevation

realWorldApplications.title: Sports Scoring
realWorldApplications.description: Golf scores relative to par, basketball score differences, football yards gained/lost

realWorldApplications.title: Time Zones
realWorldApplications.description: Time zones expressed relative to UTC (0)
realWorldApplications.example: India: UTC+5:30, New York: UTC-5, Tokyo: UTC+9

realWorldApplications.title: Stock Market
realWorldApplications.description: Stock price changes shown as positive gains or negative losses

realWorldApplications.title: Building Floors
realWorldApplications.description: Floor numbering with ground as 0, above positive, basement negative

realWorldApplications.title: Video Games
realWorldApplications.description: Health points, damage, bonuses tracked with positive and negative integers
realWorldApplications.example: +50 health gained, -20 damage taken, +100 bonus points

realWorldApplications.title: Historical Dates
realWorldApplications.description: Years before Christ (BC) are negative, years after (AD) are positive

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing which number is first in calculating difference
commonMistakes.correction: Remember: difference means first number - second number
Pay careful attention to positive and negative indicators

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting that zero pairs have no net value
commonMistakes.correction: One positive and one negative token cancel to zero
Read each question carefully and check your answer
Take time to read the scenario and understand what's being asked

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing above and below in elevation
commonMistakes.correction: Above sea level is positive, below is negative

teachingNotes.learnMode: Encourage students to experiment with different numbers in the puzzles. Use physical tokens if possible to make the abstract concepts more concrete.
teachingNotes.practiceMode: Allow students to work at their own pace. Encourage them to try again after reviewing incorrect answers.
teachingNotes.realWorldMode: Connect examples to students' own experiences. Ask them to share their own examples of integers in daily life.

accessibilityNotes: Tokens of different shapes may be used for positive and negative numbers for visually challenged students. All interactive elements have keyboard navigation support.
culturalContext: This chapter introduces concepts that were historically developed by mathematicians like Brahmagupta, whose work on multiplication and division will be explored in section 2.2.
